finding.expected: Preserve the already-added local terminalization and bounded diagnostics, but restore normal best-effort canonical failure transport for admitted Human interruption and bind interruption phase to the phase in which it actually occurs. A native-execution Ctrl+C must terminalize as EXECUTION; an interruption during Runtime verification/completion must not be mislabeled EXECUTION. Do not clean, reset, stash, commit, retry, reroute, replace the Executor, or turn the interruption into PASS. Add focused regressions covering portable failure transport and truthful phase while preserving exactly one native invocation.
finding.issue: The new KeyboardInterrupt terminalization path does not preserve existing Runtime transport semantics and does not preserve truthful failure phase. PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and REPAIR wrappers call failure persistence with transport disabled, so an admitted interruption can become terminal only in local .git/aios state without the normal portable remote failure lineage. In addition, persist_failure classifies every direct KeyboardInterrupt as EXECUTION even though the outer wrappers can also receive an interruption during Runtime verification, completion, or terminal transport. This can leave a remotely invisible correction state and can record false failure-phase truth, despite AC8 requiring interruption paths to preserve existing Runtime completion/transport semantics.
